does: Pares a vegetable into a neat barrel with curved sides, so that every piece cooks in the same time and rolls in the pan.

intro.what: Turning pares vegetables into small barrels with curved faces and tapered ends.
intro.why: It teaches you consistent starting sizes and flowing knife strokes for an even finished shape.

how: Cut the vegetable into pieces of one length, and split large ones into halves or quarters.
Hold a piece between thumb and finger and draw a small knife from end to end in one curved stroke.
Turn the piece a little and cut again, until it has even faces and tapers at both ends.
Drop potatoes into cold water as they are done, and keep the parings for a soup or a mash.

cues.text: Small barrels of one size, with smooth curved faces and blunt ends.

mistakes.mistake: Short, choppy cuts, which leave flat steps instead of a curve.
mistakes.fix: Take each face in one long stroke, turning the wrist.

mistakes.mistake: Pieces of different sizes, which cook unevenly.
mistakes.fix: Cut all the pieces to one length before you start.

quiz.question: Why begin with vegetable pieces of matching length?
choices: To keep every finished piece a different size.
To remove the need to judge thickness.
To make the finished barrels similar in size.
quiz.because: Consistent starting pieces make a matching set easier to produce.

quiz.question: How should each curved face be cut?
choices: Draw the small knife along the piece in a flowing curved stroke.
Make short downward chops across the face.
Cut deep square steps into the sides.
quiz.because: A continuous curved motion creates the smooth barrel face rather than a stepped surface.

quiz.question: Which shape is the aim?
choices: Small matching barrels with smooth curved faces.
Flat slabs with sharp square corners.
quiz.because: The turned shape has flowing sides and consistent proportions across the pieces.

quiz.question: Short cuts leave flat steps instead of a curve. What should change?
choices: Make more short abrupt cuts at the same angle.
Press down harder at the centre of each step.
Use a longer flowing stroke while turning the wrist.
quiz.because: A continuous stroke smooths the curve instead of accumulating separate flat cuts.

comes_after.why: A vegetable is peeled before it is turned.
